title: malloc usage

steps.title: Including stdio.h header
steps.explanation:
This header is needed to use `printf`.

This lesson covers the safe malloc pattern: allocate-check-use-free.

steps.title: Including stdlib.h header
steps.explanation:
This header is needed to use `malloc` and `free`.

Dynamic memory function declarations are found here.

steps.title: Defining the main function
steps.explanation:
The main frame is created.

In the following steps, we will follow the standard usage sequence for heap memory.

steps.title: Requesting heap memory allocation
steps.explanation:
`malloc(sizeof(int))` requests space for one integer on the heap.

It returns the address on success, or `NULL` on failure.

steps.title: Checking for allocation failure
steps.explanation:
We first check whether `p == NULL`.

A NULL check is the basic safety mechanism to prevent crashes.

steps.title: Printing failure message
steps.explanation: We notify the user about the allocation failure.

steps.title: Returning error code
steps.explanation:
`return 1;` indicates abnormal termination.

It is important not to continue execution after a failure.

steps.title: Storing a value in heap memory
steps.explanation: `*p = 100;` stores a value in the allocated heap space.

steps.title: Printing the heap value
steps.explanation: We read `*p` to print the stored value.

steps.title: Freeing heap memory
steps.explanation:
`free(p)` returns the used heap memory back to the system.

After freeing, you should avoid reusing the pointer.

steps.title: Successful program termination
steps.explanation:
The program terminates normally with `return 0;`.

Summary: Using malloc always includes a NULL check and free.

quiz.question:
The return type of malloc is `void*`.
What does that mean?
options: It is an address with no determined type
quiz.explanation:
`void*` means 'an address whose type is unknown'.
That is why it is standard practice to cast it like `(int*)`.

misconceptions.wrong: Memory allocated with malloc is initialized to 0
misconceptions.why:
If you need zero-initialized memory, use `calloc`.
`malloc` skips initialization for speed.

keyTakeaway: Borrow with `malloc(sizeof(type))`, check for `NULL`, and use through the pointer.
